gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns confusing a tangential exact-differential integral with the normal flux across a closed boundary. ISSUE-001 instead diagnoses an inconsistent Neumann-to-Dirichlet relation and an omitted zero-eigenvalue case in the Steklov theorem; it does not recognize the flux formula defect.

Both entries concern the complex-layer lemma, but the gold defect is the sign of the quadratic term in f_G and the resulting real-part calculation. ISSUE-002 diagnoses a different measure/formula error, replacing |d\xi| by d\xi in the double-layer definition and jump proof, without recognizing the quadratic-sign defect.

The gold issue is the incorrect weighted-transpose identity D_s=D^T, which should be H^{-1}D^T H for nonuniform arc-length weights. ISSUE-003 instead identifies omission of M from the discrete Steklov right-hand operator; it does not diagnose the adjoint-matrix weighting relation.

The gold issue concerns double application of the quadrature weight in the singular S_1^k block and requires replacing h_j^k R_j^k by |z'|R_j^k. ISSUE-003 concerns the separate omission of the M term in the Steklov pencil and gives no diagnosis of singular-block scaling.

Both entries identify that the discrete Steklov pencil omits the constant-projector term M on the right-hand side. The prediction explicitly gives the corrected operator S(I-M)+M, explains the resulting inconsistency for nonzero mean densities, and matches the gold repair restoring the constant-density zero mode.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The printed discrete Steklov equation represents S(I-M) rather than the stated modified operator S_0=S(I-M)+M because it omits the M term. Consequently it annihilates or mishandles the constant-density component and fails to represent the full Steklov problem, including the zero mode.

component_coverage.gold_component: The discrete right-hand operator omits the M term and therefore represents S(I-M) instead of S_0=S(I-M)+M.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 explicitly states that the equation uses sigma S(I-M) while the correct discrete operator is sigma[S(I-M)+M], and supplies the corrected pencil.

component_coverage.gold_component: The omission makes the pencil annihilate the constant-density component and excludes the zero Steklov mode from the full problem.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 explains the constant contribution and the resulting failure of the eigenfunction relation unless the mean vanishes, identifying the full-eigenfunction inconsistency caused by the omitted M term.
